claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim Child Benefit for my child Alex, who is 16 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Since Alex is 16 years old, I need to ask: is Alex currently in approved education or training? This would include things like:
- A-levels or equivalent
- Scottish Highers
- NVQs up to Level 3
- An approved training course (not a job contract)

If Alex has left education or training, please let me know when that happened.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in any education or training at the moment. They finished school and haven't started anything else since then.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Since Alex is 16 and has left education and is not in approved training, I have a couple more questions to understand the situation fully.

When did Alex finish school? Specifically, was it:
- Before or after the last day of February, or
- Before or after the summer holidays?

This timing is important because Child Benefit can sometimes continue for a period after a child leaves education, depending on when they left.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex left school at the end of the summer term, so just before the summer holidays started.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that detail. Let me ask a few more questions to complete the assessment.

1. Are you responsible for Alex? This means Alex lives with you, or you contribute to the cost of looking after them at least the same amount as Child Benefit would provide.

2. Do you live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me here at home. And yes, I live in the UK - we're in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Let me check the specific rules about what happens when a 16 or 17-year-old leaves education.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for your patience. I have one more important question:

Since Alex left school at 16 and is not currently in education or training, has Alex registered with either:
- A government-sponsored careers service (such as the National Careers Service), or
- The armed services?

This is important because if Alex has registered with one of these, you may be able to continue receiving Child Benefit for up to 20 weeks after leaving education.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex hasn't registered with the careers service or the armed services. They've just been at home since finishing school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:

- Alex is 16 years old
- Alex has left school (finished at the end of summer term)
- Alex is not in approved education or training
- Alex has not registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services

Unfortunately, since Alex is 16, has left education, and has not registered with a careers service or the armed services, the eligibility for Child Benefit has ended. 

Child Benefit normally continues until a child is 16, or up to age 20 if they stay in approved education or training. For 16 or 17-year-olds who leave education, Child Benefit can continue for 20 weeks **only if** they register with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services.

Let me provide you with my formal assessment:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on my assessment, I'm afraid you are **not currently eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex.

**Summary:**
- You meet the general requirements (you live in the UK and are responsible for Alex)
- However, Alex is 16 and has left education without continuing to approved training
- Alex has not registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services

**What you could do:**
If Alex registers with a government-sponsored careers service (such as the National Careers Service) or the armed services, you may be able to claim Child Benefit for up to 20 weeks from when Alex left education. Alternatively, if Alex decides to return to approved education or training (such as A-levels, a college course, or an approved training programme), you could become eligible again until Alex turns 20.

I hope this information is helpful. If you have any questions or Alex's circumstances change, please don't hesitate to contact the Child Benefit Office for further guidance.

Alex is not in approved education or training and has not registered with a careers service or the armed services. Therefore, the claimant is no longer eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.
